text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The ANZ Banking Group and London-based Standard Chartered Bank are looking into a A$24 billion stock merger that would create an Asian powerhouse bank with strong northern and southern hemisphere core businesses. The two banks have employed Goldman Sachs and Swiss Bank Corp to advise on the deal's structure. Page 1.

An extremely weak 1995 season has seen Australia's leading retailers slash inventories and go on the defensive for this year's Christmas trading. Most retailers are leaving their marketing drive for the festive season as late as possible, and many hope the expected cut in interest rates will increase spending. Page 1.

The A$157 billion worldwide personal computer industry, dominated by Microsoft and Intel, will come under challenge tomorrow when Sun Microsystems unveils its JavaStation NC, a US$500 "network computer" which is set to create an Internet-ready device that would cut corporate budgets and plug the Internet directly into the lounge room television. Page 3.

Australian Securities Commission chairman Alan Cameron said one of the Big Six accounting firms - Arthur Anderson, Coopers & Lybrand, Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu, Ernst & Young, KPMG and Price Waterhouse - could be contracted to regulate the listed Australia Stock Exchange. Page 23.

As the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission began action in the Federal Court last week against Kerry Stokes' Seven Network, Kerry Packer's Nine Network was not prepared to take on the competition watchdog in court. After day-long negotiations, the Nine Network agreed not to contest claims that programming agreements between Nine, Seven and Golden West and others had breached the Trade Practices Act. Page 23.

Battle Mountain Gold Company has dropped plans to move to 100 per cent ownership of Niugini Mining Ltd, after the North American miner indicated it was not prepared to pay more than A$4 a share for the Niugini shares it does not already own. Battle Mountain said earlier this year that it would either move to takeover Niugini or sell down its 50.5 per cent stake. Page 25.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Despite significant changes to the original legislation, Australia's peak business organisation, the Business Council of Australia, has welcomed an agreement on amendments to the Workplace Relations Bill, saying it secured progress on a significant area of economic reform and overrode initial concerns over a deal with the Democrats. Page 17.

Chief economists contacted by The Australian are happy with the agreement to pass the Workplace Relations Bill through the Senate, saying the Federal Government's labour market reforms hold potential to dramatically improve Australia's long-term economic performance. Page 17.

West Australian Resources Development Minister Barnett said the State Government is considering a switch in plant site and a change from road to rail transport for the A$1.4 billion Mid-West Iron and Steel Project in an attempt to have the project approve by next week. Page 19.

One of Australia's biggest radio communications companies, Simoco Pacific, is embarking on a roadshow in Asia. The company operated as Philips Private Mobile Radio in Asia up until about five years ago, but after competitors started to make inroads, Philips sold the operations to Simoco International earlier this year. Managing director Peter Bentley said customers in the region have remained loyal. Page 19.

Australian executives will take key roles in the restructuring of operations of international finance house Rothschild Group. Rothschild Australia chief executive Richard Lee will head internal resources banking, while chairman of the London bullion market Rob Ashley will head the global treasury. Page 19.

Permanent Trustee Australia Ltd will today begin defending itself in court actions against 23,000 investors led by the Australian Securities Commission, which is seeking A$320 million compensation on their behalf, after claims the company breached its duty by investing A$145 million in a "speculative and imprudent" building development in central Sydney. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Despite offering an interest rate of 16 per cent, Australis Media's attempts to raise funds through a secured bond issue in the United States have managed to receive commitments for only half of the US$150 million target. Consequently, Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting and United States cable operator Lenfest may be forced to contribute a large amount to the bond issue. Page 35.

An increase in the number of multinationals in Australia has led the Australian Tax Office to launch a full-scale attack on transfer pricing, or international profit shifting, making it a tax issue that should be of concern to every company with offshore subsidiaries. Page 35.

Industry figures supplied by Corporate Adviser Securities Data show that Australia's corporate sector looks to end the year on a high note, with at least A$21 billion of transactions so far this year, and several more multi-billion dollar deals on the way The increased number of transactions come as State and Federal Governments move to privatise more infrastructure and large companies follow their programmes of divesting non-core assets. Page 35.

After failing to strike a deal with United States gold producer Battle Mountain, Niugini Mining is expected to distribute its stake in Lihir Gold to its shareholders. Niugini management is considering several moves as several key shareholdings in Lihir, including that of project manager RTZ-CRA, which has 17.15 per cent, appear to be up for grabs. Page 35.

After downplaying Finance Sector Union claims that it planned to cut 5,000 jobs over the next six months, ANZ plans to close a minimum of 110 branches around the country and up to 7,000 jobs in a bid to cut costs and increase efficiencies. The bank has already started retrenching about 350 top line executives, in a move expected to cut staff costs by about A$40 million a year. Page 37.

The Command Petroleum board has recommended a A$365 million takeover offer from Scottish oil and gas independent Cairn Energy, which was deemed fair and reasonable in an independent report by merchant bankers Grant Samuel and Associates. The report value Command's shares at between 89 cents and A$1.05 a share, compared with Cairn's cash offer of A$1.10 a share. Page 37.
THE AGE

The release of this week's key economic data is likely to be overshadowed by expectations of a November cut by the Reserve Bank of official interest rates. Additionally, the latest current account, unemployment, building approvals and retail trade figure will be complicated by the release of key United States economic figures that may increase interest rates over there. Page C1.

Niugini Mining is considering distributing its stake in Lihir Gold to shareholders, after failing to agree to a deal with US miner Battle Mountain. Niugini's 17.15 per cent stake in the owner of Papua New Guinea's A$1 billion gold project looks set to be the first of key shareholdings in Lihir to be up for grabs. Page C1.

After taking up the position of national program manager for small business income last month, the Australian Taxation Office's David Butler said the office faces the challenge of improving its image with small business. Butler said small business people had to be aware of the issues behind their tax problems and his office wanted to show itself to be working with small business, rather than against it. Page C2.

Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and US cable operator Lenfest may be forced to contribute to Australis Media's A$190 million bond issue to prevent the pay TV group from being put in the hands of a receiver, after it only managed to receive commitments for about half the targeted amount, despite offering a 16 per cent interest rate. Page C3.

The latest BIS Shrapnel Building Industry Prospects report, to be released today, forecasts a four per cent fall in overall dwelling construction for 1996-97, an improvement on 1995-96's 27 percent slump in total dwelling commencements to 121,500. BIS Shrapnel's director of building services, Robert Mellor, said the recovery would be slow because of a large stock of excess dwellings. Page C3.

Waste recycler Toxfree Systems is set to float on the stockmarket and expected to raise A$15 million, which would capitalise it around A$50 million after listing. The group is emerging from the developmental stage, with strong demand for its world-leading, efficient technology for treating industrial contamination in Australia, the US and South-East Asia. Page C3.
